chapter_theme: Songs at Thiruttani (திருத்தணிகை, 2 of 5): the poet turns from women who deceive and rob, from the false pot of the body, and from sectarians who chase gods and gold back into the womb, and asks for the feet, release and the gift of praise; four songs are love laments for a girl wasting for Murugan, and one, 269, praises the Thiruppugazh itself as fire. The praise returns often to Murugan as teacher of Siva and as Sambandar who routed the Jains.
structure_note: Courtesan and desire songs (255, 260, 264, 266, 267); the body and birth (258); sectarians and false company (257, 261); the gift of praise and the poet's lowliness (263, 269); akam laments in another voice asking for Murugan's garland or arm (256, 259, 262, 265); and 268, a thanksgiving for a teaching received in which Murugan writes Valli's beauty on the madal.

255.reading: The poet describes women who loosen their dark hair, glance with fish eyes, jingle bangles and chains and shimmer their garments, and the deceitful ones (கவட்டர்) who bow only to destroy the heart; he asks Murugan to look on him so that, free of their company, he may bathe in the sea of austerity, become his servant and live in his shrine with a glad mind. The praise names Murugan the guru of his father Siva, who burnt the cities, flayed the elephant and wears ash, the poet of nectar-praise in a kadamba garland, and the vel that dusts the demons' horses and elephants, at Thiruttani where the hunter girl rejoices.
255.nuance: உனக்கு அடிமையுற்று உன் தலத்தினில் இருக்கும்படி: the remedy asked is to live at the shrine itself as the Lord's servant, a concrete hope beside the inward bath in தவக்கடல். எனப்பன் குருநாதா calls Murugan 'guru of my father', the poet claiming Siva as his own father.

256.reading: In the voice of one watching over a lovesick girl, the singer asks that the creeper-waisted girl not perish under the women's taunts and the noise of bangles, the dark cloud and swelling water on the shore, and the many killing arrows of Kama, and that Murugan graciously give her his cool garland of kura and kadamba flowers. The praise names the vel that the lords of Uma, Saraswati and Lakshmi worship, the chest where Valli of the millet field and the heavenly deer Devayanai dwell, and the lord who rides his peacock daily at Thanigai so that the loneliness of the lonely ends.
256.nuance: The request for the god's garland is the akam convention of the girl asking for her lover's token. கலைமடவார் தஞ் சிலை may be the women's gossip (சிலை as sound) or their bow-like brows, so whether this is அலர் is uncertain. தனியவர் கூருந் தனிகெட: the god rides out to end the solitude of the lonely, which turns the praise back to the girl.

257.reading: The poet asks why the deceitful siddhas and those confused by the six sects, who consecrate many gods, fix names and set up images, and seek wealth for necklaces, signet rings, bangles and chains, should wander dividing themselves only to enter the womb again; will they not understand a little the fame of the Lord's feet, which stand one with everything and yet apart? The praise is of the vel that churned the eight peaks and the sea, cut Surapadman and bathed in his blood, of Valli bowing in shame in the millet field, and of Thiruttani with its golden walls, lord of Sruti and Tamil poetry.
257.nuance: சகலத்தும் ஒற்றைபட்டு அயல்பட்டு நிற்கும்: the Lord is at once one with all things and other than them, the doctrine of pervasion with transcendence, set against the sects' many installed gods. The jewels named (சவடி, இலச்சினை, சரி, சரப்பளி) make the sectarians' religion a trade. Whether the wanderer of the first lines is the poet or the sectarians depends on how உழல்வானேன் is taken.

258.reading: Not knowing how to draw near the anklet feet, his mind on women with heavy breasts and dark kohl eyes, the poet asks Murugan to cut off this birth that bears the false pot of flesh, skin and semen, a bellows that is home to the troop of diseases, and to give him release every day. The praise names the vel that fought the elephant-borne demon, the Kumaresa of the cock banner whose feet trample the pride of mountains, and the embrace of the hunter girl, at Thiruttani of pearls.
258.nuance: இனப்பிணிக் கணத்தினுக்கு இருப்பு, துருத்தி, பொய்க் கடம்: three images of the body in one line, a lodging for diseases, a bellows of breath, a false pot. The plea asks for release daily (நித்தம் முத்தி), as if it must be renewed.

259.reading: A short love lament: the singer asks whether, because of the roaring dark sea, the moon that rises red as fire, and the arrows Kama shoots from his sugarcane bow, a girl should be stopped here and her body grow slack. The praise names Murugan the husband of the girl who once guarded the millet, Kandavel shining on the hill of Thiruttani, and the lord of the three gods who create, protect and destroy.
259.nuance: The torments are the classical night machinery, sea, moon and Kama's cane bow, as in 24; the moon is called hot (சிவத்து அங்கி வாய்த்து எழு திங்கள்), the cool moon turned to fire by longing. ஒருத்தி is in the third person, so the speaker is a mother or friend. பனைக்கரக் கயத்து அண்டர் போற்றிய மங்கைபாகா is hard to place: it may name Siva or Murugan.

260.reading: The poet lists the courtesans: actresses of deceit who drop their garments, bodies full of disease, sweet talkers who embrace on the bed until the heart melts for money, who fight with loveless infatuation, embrace whoever gives more as if he were an old friend, and steal like arrows with their eyes; he asks whether a day will come when, not thinking of them, he thinks of Murugan coming on the peacock to tell him the way to the state of release. The praise names the vel that dusted the demons who harried Vishnu, Brahma and the gods, the husband of the hunter girl, and the lord at Thanigai whose lotus feet are reached by those of dharma, Veda, patience, unwavering austerity and wisdom.
260.nuance: அதிகமா ஒரு பொருள் தருபவரொடு பழைய பேரென இதமுற அணைபவர்: the courtesan treats the highest payer as an old friend, the stock charge of money for love. The praise ends with a long list of who reach the feet, the devotees' virtues answering the women's vices.

261.reading: The poet asks whether, having fallen in with liars, followers of the senses, blind fools whose eyes do not look to end birth, thieves and sectarian disputants, knowing nothing, weary and sinking in the sea of the womb, he will rise in understanding and reach the paired feet. The praise identifies Murugan with Sambandar, the poet of the Kaundinya line at Pugali who spread holy ash to cure the Pandyan's fever and crushed the Jains, and names him the son of Siva who burnt the cities with a laugh, lord at Seruttani where the kuvalai blooms daily in the spring.
261.nuance: The plea turns on company: the bad are named in a string of types (கிருதர், பொறிவழிச் செறிஞர், குருடர், திருடர், சமயதர்க்கிகள்), and to keep company with them is already to sink. The praise is Sambandar's story told of Murugan: the Pandyan (செழியன்) freed of fever by holy ash at Madurai and the shaven-headed Jains (பறிதலைப் சமணர்) defeated.

262.reading: A love lament: the cuckoo torments the cuckoo-voiced girl, Kama's flower arrows kill, the cool white moon and the fire of her breasts burn, the wind and the roaring sea and the women's gossip assail her, and her arm grows weak; the singer asks whether she may not be given Murugan's own arm to embrace. The praise names the hero who fought until the mountain shook, the chest that joins the hunter girl's breast, Thanigai where the crescent bows in the cool groves, and Murugan of Sengazhani who told the meaning to the Supreme when he bowed.
262.nuance: பொருமங்கையர் உக்கு அலர்: the women's gossip is one of the torments, alongside cuckoo, moon and sea. பரமன் பணியப் பொருள் அன்று அருளிற் பகர்: Siva bowed and Murugan told him the meaning, the teaching of 6 and 24, here without naming Om. The speaker may be the girl or one who watches her.

263.reading: The poet asks not to wander born as sparrow, kite, jackal, forest beast, worm, fish, elephant and tree, nor to bathe at Kumari with a sorrowing mind and be mocked by many as a diseased wretch; he will not seek ornaments, elephants, horses, silks and golden vessels, and asks instead that, as Murugan's feet suffice for his dwelling, he be given the Thiruppugazh that dwells in them. The praise, after drum syllables of battle, names Siva who burnt the cities with his eye and cut Brahma's head, and Murugan who impaled the Jains and dances at Thiruttani with Valli and Devayanai.
263.nuance: The list of creatures reads as the births the poet fears (திரி உறவாகா), though it may be a list of insults the crowd would throw. உனது பதச்சரண் மருவு திருப்புகழ்: the poet asks for his own book's name, praise that rests in the feet. அமணர் உடற்கெட வசியில் அழுத்தி is again the impaling of the Jains, Sambandar's story told of Murugan, as in 261. The lines on the feet and the waterfall (வரிய பதத்தினில் நருவி) are hard to divide.

264.reading: The poet asks whether it is fit to be kin to the common women who loosen their hair, roll their gemmed breasts, whirl their fish eyes, arch their crescent brows, laugh, kindle infatuation, sway as they walk and, feeding his desire, destroy his austerity. The praise names Siva who bent the bow and burnt the three cities, wore the axe and the tiger and elephant skins, and held the poison in his throat so the gods survived, and calls Murugan the one who told the meaning to that matted-haired god, and the hero bathed in infatuation for the hunter girl at Thiruttani.
264.nuance: பொதுமாதர்: common women, but money is not named, so the charge is desire, not trade. தவத்து அழிப்பவர்: what they destroy is austerity. சடைக் கடவுட் சிறக்கப் பொருட் பகர்வோனே is the teaching of Siva, without naming Om.

265.reading: A love lament: the singer asks that this girl not weaken under the crescent moon, the umbrella-crown of Kama who shot the kuvalai arrow, and under the cuckoo, and that Murugan, who has drawn her close and embraced her shoulders in love, give her his sweet garland of compassion to wear in peerless beauty. The praise names the vel that fought the golden mountain until the eight elephants cried, the chest that rises to embrace the girl, and Thiruttani where heaps of coral and pearls lie like hills by the fields and conches crowd.
265.nuance: இவளை: 'this girl', so the voice is a mother or friend pleading for her. The garland is called கருணைக்கு இனிமைத் தொடை, a garland of compassion: the love token is also grace. The crescent as Kama's royal umbrella (குடை) is a striking image.

266.reading: The poet describes courtesans who loosen and retie their hair, paint their eyes and deal double, press their breasts on a man's shoulders, leave crescent nail-marks, speak desire for many days to get the money given, cry as if forsaken, and when the money ends leave him groaning at the door; he asks how, without the compassionate feet that would take him from their side, he can enter the good state. The praise names Murugan nephew of Achyuta of the Gandiva and of Rama with the monkey army, younger brother of the elephant-faced god who ate fruits and sugar, and the one who stood as the vengai tree to unite with honey-voiced Valli, at the Thiruttani hill of sugarcane and kuvalai springs.
266.nuance: பொருள்தீரில் ஏங்கியிடக் கடையில் தளிவைப்பவர்: the man left groaning at the door once his money ends, the formula of 33. ஈந்திலை: 'you have not given', a reproach to the Lord, not only a plea. In the praise Vishnu is named as Krishna with Arjuna's bow (காண்டிப அச்சுதன்).

267.reading: The poet describes women who bewilder with eyes sharper than spears, call with their breasts, draw a man to the flower bed, drink from his lips, loosen their hair and scold while their ear ornaments fall in play, and asks whether the strife of dwelling rejoicing among these infatuating women, as in Yama's forest-town, will not end. The praise names the vel that killed Sura amid drums and the sound of Vedas and Agamas, the guru who gave the great teaching in the holy ear of Siva who burnt Kama with a laugh, and the lord who embraces Valli, given by Vishnu, at Thiruttani.
267.nuance: நம கானூர் உறைக் கலகம் is uncertain: it may be the turmoil of dwelling in Yama's town (நமன் கானூர்) or be split otherwise. தாதா திருச்செவியில் மாபோதகத்தை அருள் குருநாதா: the teaching whispered in Siva's ear, the Om story, though Om is not named. மாலோன் அளித்த வளி makes Valli Vishnu's daughter.

268.reading: The poet thanks the guru who dwells at the foot of the kura tree, in the lotus of devotees' hearts and at the crown of the Vedas, who told him the way that sectarian disputants cannot reach and others never meet, 'this is the tradition', and gave the great grace of his anklet feet; he will not forget it in dream or waking. The praise names Murugan son of Siva of the matted hair, and the lord who painted on the madal Valli's lotus feet, bamboo arms, moon face, musk-dark breasts, honey speech and smile, red as the cochineal insect and green as emerald.
268.nuance: A song of thanksgiving rather than plea: the poet speaks of a teaching already received, தனது என வரும் ஒரு சம்ப்ரதாயம், a tradition that comes as one's own, beyond the reach of சமய விரோத தந்த்ர வாதிகள். குரவடி may recall Siva teaching under the kura tree. The ending makes Murugan the lover who rides the madal, painting the beloved's form on it, the akam convention turned on the god. கொந்து காவென is obscure.

269.reading: The poet declares that the Thiruppugazh is fire to the heads of the angry, the clans of enemies, the lives of destroyers, and to those who laugh and those who blame; it grants what one thinks, melts the mind, cuts the womb of darkness so that one is not born, burns fire itself and breaks mountains, and he asks for the act of speaking that full praise. The praise, in drum syllables, shows the vel that destroyed the Suras and burnt the mountain with a laugh, and Murugan delighting in the hunter girl at Thiruttani.
269.nuance: The book praises its own name: திருப்புகழ் is given the powers of a mantra, to burn enemies, fulfil desire and end birth. நெருப்பையும் எரிக்கும்: it burns even fire. The plea is not for the praise itself but for the act of speaking it (உரைக்கும் செயல்).

links.note: Both say the six sects lead back to birth: in Tirumular they perish where they stand, not knowing the way to leave the earth, and in 257 the sectarians who install many gods wander only to enter the womb again.

Both call the body a pot to turn the mind from women. The Naladiyar's pot is the woman's body seeping filth; 258 turns the image on the poet's own body, a false pot of flesh, skin and semen, and asks not just to leave desire but to have that birth cut off.

Both make the town's gossip feed love's sickness: the Kural's woman calls it the manure of her disease, and in 262 the women's talk is one of the torments, with cuckoo, moon and sea, that waste the girl's arm.
Both laments end by asking Murugan to give the wasting girl his garland; 265 calls it a garland of compassion, so the love token becomes grace.
The same formula of the courtesan's love that lasts as long as the money: in 33 the man is beaten from the door when it ends, in 266 he is left groaning there.
Both identify Murugan with Sambandar defeating the Jains: 261 tells the cure of the Pandyan and the crushing of the Jains, 263 the impaling.

source_issues: Song 255: மினுக்யும் (line 4) has lost a letter, probably மினுக்கியும்.
Song 256: புமணி (line 4) probably பூமணி; கநவன (line 6) is garbled, probably a lost letter as in songs 21 and 33.
Song 261: one corrupt character, in கருக்கடலு஡டே (line 6), read as கடலூடே.
Song 266: one corrupt character, ஡ணங்கிசை (line 9), probably ரீ, giving இட்டவரீங்கிசை (இட்டவர் ஈங்கு இசை).
Song 267: one corrupt character, in கானு஡ர் (line 8), read as கானூர்.
Song 268: two corrupt characters, சஞ்ச஡ண (line 10), probably சஞ்சரீக (bee), and செம்பொனு஡புற (line 18), probably செம்பொன் நூபுர (golden anklet).
